post.caption: Jackie Kennedy's famous pearls were faux. Her three strand pearl necklace shows up in many photographs from the early 1960s, and it was made of simulated pearls. Her estate was sold at Sotheby's in New York in April 1996, and the necklace was expected to fetch five hundred to seven hundred dollars. It sold for $211,500 to the Franklin Mint, a company near Philadelphia, which later sold about 130,000 copies. The original is kept in the Smithsonian in Washington.
